chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not prescribe for women any making up (of missed fasts/prayers) nor any fasting except what He made obligatory upon them, which is the fasting of Ramadan, nor any prayer except what He made obligatory upon them, which is the prayer of the day and night, except for that which exempts them due to an excuse, such as menstruation and postpartum bleeding.
ai.seo_question: Do women need to make up missed prayers and fasts?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling in *Kamal al-Din*, highlighting the juristic consensus that women’s menstrual and postpartum periods constitute a valid excuse for missing prayers but do not impose the obligation of *qada* (making up) them, distinguishing this from fasting. This position contrasts with the Hanafi view and underscores the Shia understanding that prayer is tied to the state of ritual purity rather than the passage of time, whereas fasting is tied to the calendar. The narration reinforces the principle that the exemption from prayer during menstruation is a mercy that removes the burden entirely, without requiring compensation.
